start_here: Say to your AI: "Write a sign-in code message for sam@example.com, subject 'Your code', text '123456', kind sign-in-code, as a row of my sign-in-code list with key k1, using my door config file door.json." It runs tool:deliver-to-list on your computer and tells you the row was written.
no_lists_because: It names no fixed list: it writes one row into whichever list row type you pass in row_type, so the list is your own choice and not part of the tool.
instructions: 1. Have your door config file ready (for example door.json) and pick the row type of the list that should receive the message (for example sign-in-code).

2. Say "Write this message as a row of my list" and give your AI to, subject, text, kind and an idempotencyKey; the AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:deliver-to-list}, because it runs on your computer.
3. The AI runs the row's command from the root of the Workshop checkout with the message as one JSON object on standard input.

4. Read the last JSON line: {"sent":[{"messageId":"k1"}]} means the row was written; {"sent":[{"error":...}],"unknown":false} means the door refused it; {"sent":[{"unknown":true}],"unknown":true} means it may have been written, so send again with the same key (the same key writes the same row).
5. Exit code 0 means written, 2 means not written or unknown.

worked_examples.title: A sign-in code written as one row
worked_examples.ask: Write a sign-in code message for sam@example.com as a row of my sign-in-code list.
worked_examples.given: From tools/deliver-to-list/test/deliver-to-list.test.mjs and read from tools/deliver-to-list/do-work/deliver-to-list.mjs: the AI runs, from the Workshop checkout root, echo '{"config":"door.json","row_type":"sign-in-code","to":"sam@example.com","subject":"Your code","text":"123456","kind":"sign-in-code","idempotencyKey":"k1"}' | node tools/deliver-to-list/do-work/deliver-to-list.mjs. The door accepts the write of one row with id k1 and type record:sign-in-code, whose value is {to: sam@example.com, subject: Your code, text: 123456, kind: sign-in-code, at: <the time of the send>}.
